thread:
maria: Heads-up — CI perf alert after merging PR 3499 (adaptive kernel + batching tweaks). Canary variant B is showing a big tail spike :frowning:
aj: link? can you paste the perf query/output? :eyes:
maria: https://redwood.tools/telemetry/compare?range=10m

maria: Quick query I ran:
```sql
-- p99 latency for canary variants (last 10m)
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) as p99
FROM inference_requests
WHERE release = 'canary' AND variant = 'B' AND minute > now() - interval '10 minutes';
```

maria: Output: p99 = 420ms (baseline for variant A ~180ms)
liam: that's ~2.3x, ouch. Did CI show the regression before the rollout?
zoe: CI perf job flagged a small bump but it stayed under threshold. The canary rollout has more realistic seq length distribution so it probably exposed KV/cache edge-case.
rob: Observed patterns: higher KV miss rate and more small batches. Looks like batching heuristic is favoring smaller windows under bursty arrival. KV miss + smaller batches -> more kernel context switches -> tail.
zoe: I bisected locally. git bisect points to commit abc123 from PR 3499 — the change that adjusts eviction TTL and batch window heuristic.
```bash
$ git bisect start
$ git bisect bad HEAD
$ git bisect good v1.34.2
# bisect: found commit abc123
# commit: tweak-kv-ttl-and-adaptive-batching (PR 3499)
```

aj: If bisect landed on that, we need an immediate mitigant. Options: revert PR 3499, tweak TTL back, or pause canary.
maria: We already have autopause checks but they were tuned for error-rate and severe latency. Need a p99-based gate. Right now autopause threshold is p95>300ms for 10m which didn't trip.
rob: Suggest new guard: if p99 increases >1.5x baseline for 5m OR if KV miss rate increases >3x for 5m -> autopause. Also add an early pause when small-batch ratio >30% and p99 up.
liam: Agree. Also add an immediate short-term rollback while we iterate. I'll prepare a revert PR.
zoe: I can push a hotfix to restore previous TTL + keep batching improvements behind a feature flag. That should reduce KV churn.
aj: For rollout system: propose auto-pause policy changes and an action to auto-trigger a rollback job that runs a fast canary revert (route 0% to variant B) when autopause fires. We should avoid manual steps for high-severity perf regressions.
rob: +1. We should also add a CI perf test that runs the realistic sequence-length mix fixture (the one that exposed this) and asserts p99 < 250ms.

maria: Rolling plan: 1) add autopause rule (p99-based) 2) trigger auto-rollback if autopause persists >3m 3) merge hotfix revert PR for TTL 4) add CI perf test and backfill alerts.
aj: I'll draft the autopause change and open a small ops PR to the rollout config.
liam: Revert PR created: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3501 (revert PR 3499). Please review quick. :shipit:

sre-bot: [incident] perf-regression-detected: canary/variant-B p99 increased to 420ms at 2025-09-12T14:12:03Z. Autopause rule evaluation pending.
deploy-bot: Autopause evaluation triggered for canary-v2. Current window: 5m.

deploy-bot: Autopause triggered — pausing rollout (variant B) and routing all new traffic to variant A. Action: queued rollback job #rb-982. :white_check_mark:
maria: Nice, autopause worked this time.
zoe: I'm going to validate that reverting TTL brings p99 down in a local canary. If yes, we ship revert and re-run the adaptive batching behind a flag.
aj: Action items:
- aj: PR for autopause/p99 rule & auto-rollback hook (owner)
- liam: expedite revert PR 3501 and coordinate deploy (owner)
- zoe: prepare hotfix and feature-flag plan + perf test (owner)
- rob: add telemetry alarm for KV-miss-rate anomaly (owner)
- maria: postmortem draft and timeline (owner)

liam: FYI I'll also add a shortterm metric: small-batch-ratio (batches <= 4) so we can gate on that in future.
maria: Thanks all. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
rob: post-deploy note — once reverted, let's run the stress fixture for 1h before re-enabling the adaptive batching flag.
maria: agreed.
sre-bot: incident update: variant B paused, rollback job #rb-982 completed, canary back to baseline. p99 trending down to 175ms (5m).
aj: closing loop — we'll follow up with the postmortem and CI test changes.
